154. **The cover of each change is light that pours out of the globe, not a dark room.** (After the review, 13:28 UTC Nov 26; logged 14:00.) The cover that hides the swap of the base, the dressing and the backdrop was built on my own first route ("the room falls away from it, as a camera's exposure does", "a near silhouette"). What stood in the sheets of `bbc967b4` was a blackout: for about ten frames of each change (shake-1: frames 670 to 681, and the same place in the other three) a pale ball with a soft halo on a black frame, with no table, no base and no lamp. Three things are wrong with it. `kit/04-LOOK.md` section 5: "The slab is near black, not black. The darkest part of any frame still has tone." `kit/02-SUBJECT.md` line 141 asks for the outside to change "inside a short bloom of the new season's light pouring out of the globe", and a glass bright enough to flare lit nothing around it. And the only sign of light left was the lens glare, the same flat disc in all four changes. Chosen: the same cover with the room still there. A pool of the new season's light on the table round the foot, strongest at the foot and falling off with distance, with its mirror image; the base lit from above; the lamps of the backdrop fall but do not go out; no frame holds a patch of true black (fewer than 1 pixel in 100 with a channel sum under 4 in every frame of the four windows); the swap stays unseen as jobs 1 to 6 won it; each change has its own colour of light; the app's own path draws the same at one sample. If a part cannot be had together with the unseen swap, the unseen swap wins and the builder says which frame shows what. Brief `tools/briefs/p6/change-7.md` (`9129a940`), job 7 of `change_finisher` on `agent/p6-change`, limit 80 minutes with a first state inside 45. I look at the before and after sheets myself before the merge. The slip is mine: I asked for "near dark" and did not look at the cover's frames at full size before I called the route good.

155. **At the final tier the number of samples of a frame follows its motion.** (After the review, 13:51 UTC Nov 26; logged 14:00; open item 238.) A film frame is the mean of N pictures at N moments inside the shutter (`picture` in `src/capture/showcase.ts`; `tiers.final.samplesPerFrame` 24; `film.shutterDegrees` 180). In a shake at 3840 x 2160 the ball travels about 100 pixels inside one shutter, so the 24 moments lie about 4 pixels apart and a lamp 2 to 3 pixels wide shows as a row of copies. Three routes were weighed. More samples everywhere: four times the cost of every frame of the masters for a fault that only moving frames have. A blur laid over the picture along the motion: it would smear the glass's own edges and the storm's strokes a second time, and the kit draws motion blur from the shutter, each sample at its own moment (`kit/04-LOOK.md` lines 44 and 66), not by a filter. Chosen: `samples = clamp(ceil(travelPx / spacingPx), samplesPerFrame, maxSamplesPerFrame)`, with `travelPx` the largest travel on screen of the ball inside that frame's shutter, under `tiers.final.motion` in the config (start: 1.5 pixels and 96). A frame without motion gets 24 samples as before and must stay the same picture bit for bit; the other tiers do not change; the count is a pure function of the frame, so two machines draw the same picture. The cost falls on the four shakes (576 of film B's 3600 frames); the builder measures it before the freeze and the farm's ranges are cut with it. Brief `tools/briefs/p6/blur.md` (`184adfbc`), branch `agent/p6-blur`, one builder on a farm machine (the former `render_env_prober`). The builder may say before building that its measure shows a better route. This goes past the letter of `kit/05-ARCHITECTURE.md` line 87 ("A computed picture is the average of `tiers.<tier>.samplesPerFrame` samples"): at the final tier a moving frame becomes the average of more samples than that, never fewer. The count stays in the config beside the tier, and the departure goes into the last report.

37. Sound, `shake-winter`: no take fits after the three the cue is allowed (20:31 UTC, Phase 3). Its line is "Liquid sloshing and churning inside glass, with snow hiss and tiny bells for winter". Take 1: a spoon stirring a glass. Take 2: ice cubes or dice shaken in a container with liquid sloshing in glass, no hiss and no bells. Take 3 (water in a sealed bottle shaken six times with a strap of small sleigh bells): small sleigh bells shaken four times in open air, 59 % of the energy above 8 kHz and nothing under 1 kHz, no water. The tool gives one of the two materials a prompt names, never both. So the winter shake is silent, as the winter hold (`amb-winter`) and the crackle of the landing (item 9) are. What to try next, in a review round that buys takes: ask for the water alone and the bells alone as two takes and let the chain lay them together, which the kit's one file per cue does not forbid but its take count does today.

The window is frames 648 to 683 and the outside span 672.2 to 677.8. What to try next: in the `change` unit's fix pass, hold the storm's and the background lights' turn to spring until the base's span begins, so that frame 666 is one season, then look at every frame from 660 to 683 at the review tier. Take the frost off the table and lay the petals on it with a gust and not where they lie; the handover asks for a blow-in clock in `src/seasons/spring/slab.ts` for that. `[shared: change]`

125. **The arrival is a reveal: the crown and the tulips stand finished at the landing behind a fading pink veil, and the grass comes in as a wipe across pale ground from frame 760 to 830.** (Round 14, R4 #2, severe; `set-B-04.jpg`, with `set-B-01.jpg` to `set-B-06.jpg`, the sheets of the arrival of `shake-1`, frames 720 to 850, review tier. 126. **Item 72 again: when the globe lifts, the mirror image of the base goes out, a flat olive-green oval stands in its place from frame 680 to 706, the image snaps back at the landing, and the frost on the table never stirs.** (Round 14, R4 #3, major; `set-A-01.jpg`, the sheet across `shake-1`, winter into spring, from `hero`, review tier, frames 602 to 718, and `set-B-01.jpg`, frame 720. The frost that should stir is winter's dressing and goes with item 72. Polish round 1 (2026-11-25, 14:27 to 17:38 UTC): mended on shake 1. `agent/p5-surface`, merged as `90b1b484`: under a lifted globe the surface mirrors the foot's dark underside and the base, displaced by the gap, and the shadow opens with the lift. The dressing on the table still does not stir (the second half of item 161). Polish round 2: `surface_finisher`. `[shared: surface, shake]`

127. **Item 81 again: the shake reads light and mechanical: a low lift, even strokes, little tilt, a wide stroke at frame 680 after the strokes had damped, and a stall in the air from frame 692 to 706.** (Round 14, R4 #4, major; `set-A-01.jpg`, the sheet across `shake-1`, winter into spring, from `hero`, review tier, frames 588 to 718. 128. **At rest the petals in the liquid never thin: nine to ten seconds after the landing a dense flurry of large petals still hangs in the dome, and none are seen to gather on the roof or the grass.** (Round 14, R4 #5, major; `set-C-01.jpg`, the sheet of the film's hold on spring, review tier, frames 928 to 1294. Check on the hold's sheet at frames 1190 to 1294, and run the rest still's measures again.

129. **Item 82 again: two broad, hard white reflections at the upper right and an even grey-violet band round the glass.** (Round 16, R1 #1, severe; `set-A-01-a.jpg`, the rest pair: the approved `fall-rest.png` beside the still `fall-rest` from `hero`, hd, final; "in both keys". R3 part 2, on "crop 2, the upper-right shoulder reflection": "the secondary white highlight ends in a sharply pinched bright tip and reads like an opaque stripe over the miniature rather than a reflection on the glass" Its fix: "soften the highlight falloff and let its intensity change with the curvature while retaining the separate thin outer glass edge" Tried: `fall_air3` took the season's share, the colour of the key light (`e0cd067`: "key [1, 0.9, 0.78] at 0.5"), and tested fall's sky against the rim: "The blue fringe on the silhouette and the thick rim did NOT move with fall's sky (tested [0.097, 0.1, 0.07], reverted): they are the shared shell". Then the two things R1 names that the approved fall image has: broken warm glints at the sides and a milky green edge low on the glass. Polish round 1 (2026-11-25, 14:27 to 17:38 UTC): mended in the keys of spring, summer and fall. `agent/p5-glass`, merged as `610b48fc`: the thick ring, the cyan line and the hard white reflection give way to a thin edge and one soft reflection; seen by the Builder on main's eight keys at the final tier beside the kept ones at 18:00 UTC (`out/work/keysB/`). Left: a thin dark outline round the glass. No critic has judged the new keys yet: polish round 1's R1 check on them was ordered at 18:03, and Round 19 follows. Polish round 2: `glass_finisher_b`. `[shared: glass]`

130. **Item 74 again in part: half a second after the landing the storm is broad orange smears and green bands on a steep diagonal, where the approved image has many thin bright streaks that sweep sideways.** (Round 16, R1 #2, severe; `set-B-01-a.jpg`, the landed pair: the approved `fall-shake.png` beside the still `fall-shake`, the landed state from `hero`, hd, final. Also Round 13, R1 #6, major; Round 10, R1 #15 and #16, severe.) The target has more numerous thin, bright streaks and smaller moving fragments distributed through the volume; the motion sweeps more laterally across the miniature and veils it more evenly." Both builders name what is left. `kinds3`: "Fall's storm: trails are straight spokes, not silky arcs; no large blurred leaf shapes; green haze thicker than approved (not mine)." `fall_air3`: "Storm fog: thin ribbons now, but finer and dimmer than the approved's fewer broad bright bands." The steep diagonal is the liquid's roll axis, one constant for all four seasons (item 74); nothing was changed there. What to try next: in fall's own files, more and thinner trails at several depths with smaller heads (`CARD.line` in `src/particles/draw/looks.ts`: `share`, `leafStretch`, `widePx`, `deep`) and fewer large near leaves in the landed state. In the polish rounds the roll axis as item 74 says, then the storm tuned again with M4 and M5. The shape of a trail is item 131, the light behind the storm item 147. `[shared: liquid, the direction of the storm only]`

131. **The storm's trails are stiff straight white rods, laid over leaves and points of light that are not blurred at all.** (Round 16, R3 part 1 #1, severe; `set-B-01.jpg`, the still `fall-shake`, the landed state from `hero`, hd, final; "also set-B-02.jpg crops 1-6 and set-B-03.jpg crop 7". New in these words; Round 13's R3 part 1 #1, major, was that the streaks cross the walls and the trunk.) R3 part 1: "motion blur is faked with stiff, straight white line and rod streaks layered over crisp, completely unblurred leaves and sharp pinprick light dots moving in the same current" Its fix: "remove the separate straight streak geometry and render true curved velocity motion blur consistently across all swirling leaves and light particles" Tried: the trails are `kinds3`'s (`src/particles/draw/**`). For Round 13 it made fall's trails longer (`bb54623`) and gave each trail its own depth along its length (`56b30fd`), and it reports: "trails are straight spokes, not silky arcs; no large blurred leaf shapes". The trails are drawn along each particle's velocity; `/root` ruled at 07:31 that they are not drawn flatter than their paths. What to try next: bend each trail along the particle's path across the exposure (two or three joined pieces through its places at the start, the middle and the end of the shutter), and stretch and soften the leaf cards and the ember points by the same velocity, so that everything in one current is blurred alike. The first half of the fix, removing the streaks, is Declined issue 29.

132. **The three faces on the base are carved differently from the approved ones.** (Round 16, R1 #3, severe; `set-A-01-a.jpg`, the rest pair; "in both keys". The candidate faces also have less visible orange rind texture around the cutouts." What to try next: trace the eyes, the nose and the mouth of each face from `references/approved/fall-rest.png` where no stem covers them and draw them again in `maps.mjs`, first the middle face's eyes and teeth and the right face's broad curved grin, as R1 names them. Keep every face clear of the thorns (the kit's fall table: "each face clear of the thorns"). The depth of the cuts and the rind is item 134.

133. **The crack is kinked straight segments, and one branch is a thick straight white strip with a square end.** (Round 16, R3 part 1 #2, severe; `set-C-01.jpg`, the still `fall-interior`, the rest state from `interior`, hd, final; "also set-C-02.jpg crops 1-2 and set-A-02.jpg crops 3, 6". R3 part 1: "the crack is built from kinked straight polygon segments with one branch dropping down as a thick, ruler-straight white strip that terminates in a blunt square cut" Its fix: "replace the straight strip with a fine, irregular branching fracture inside the curved glass shell with internal edge refraction and tapered hairline tips" Tried: `fall_air3` (`c6cc937`: "the crack bows between its traced points, warmer, lit in beads"; `d3e070e`: "crack faint between its lit stretches"). It booked Round 13's issue as "fixed (c6cc937, d3e070e): bowed, lit in stretches; no refraction". Its handover: "One crack with two arms, bowed between the traced points, lit in stretches. No refraction of what lies behind it and no fine splinters at the hub." Its looks were "hero, draft hd, a few macro"; it lists none from `interior`, the camera of this critic's still. What to try next: look at the crack from `interior` first. Then, in `look.crack` of `src/seasons/fall/glass.ts`: let the width taper to nothing at every tip (`widthMm` 0.09, `edgeMm` 0.055), shorten the pieces so that no straight one shows (`stepMm` 1.6, `bowMm` 0.5), add the fine splinters at the hub, and shift what is seen behind the crack a little along its edge.

134. **The faces are flat bright cutouts with no depth, and they put no warm light on the vines, the wax or the base round them.** (Round 16, R3 part 1 #3, major; `set-A-03.jpg`, crops 8, 9, 10, native size crops of `fall-rest` from `hero`; "also set-B-03.jpg crops 8, 9, 10". R3 part 2 #3, major; `set-E-02.jpg`, crops 2 and 3, native size crops of `fall-surface`, the rest state from `surface`, hd, final. Also Round 10, R1 #12, major, R3 part 1 #7, major, and R3 part 2 #7, minor.) R3 part 1: "the glowing eyes and mouths are flat bright cutouts with no carved rind depth, and they cast zero warm glow or bounce light onto the adjacent dark vines, wax drips, or stone base" Its fix: "give the carved openings wall thickness into a lit hollow cavity and emit local warm light so surrounding vines, wax, and stone pick up orange bounce illumination" R3 part 2: "the bright eyes and teeth read as flat emissive shapes on dark shells; there is little visible cut depth or warm spill onto the nearest vines and base" Its fix: "give the cutouts visible inner walls and let the warm interior light graze the openings and nearby surfaces" Tried: `fall_base3` raised the faces' light on the vines as far as it held: "`baseCandle = mix(baseCandle, 13.0, baseStrand)` in `base.ts`; higher turned the vines orange plastic at 20". It lists "Faces light the vines round them less than approved" as still wrong. No report names an inner wall in the cuts. What to try next: model the inner wall of each cut as a rind lit orange from inside (`assets-src/base-fall/mesh.mjs`), and light the vines and the wax by their distance from each face with a fast falloff, in place of one level for every vine, so that the nearest thorns turn orange and the rest stay black. The outlines of the carvings are item 132.

135. **At rest the embers are one even golden field with large amber discs that are flat and hard-edged, and the leaves and the bats afloat are too large.** (Round 16, R1 #4, major; `set-A-02-a.jpg`, crops of the rest pair; "resting liquid, clear space above the cottage and tree". R3 part 2 #4, major; `set-D-03.jpg`, crop 7, native size crops of `fall-base`, the rest state from `low`, hd, final. Also Round 13, R1 #5, major; Round 10, R1 #1 and #5, severe, and R3 part 2 #5, minor.) R1: "The candidate has a much more uniform golden star field with large sharp-edged amber circles and conspicuously large dark bats. The target has more isolated sharp ember cores, a wider spread of softness and brightness with depth, smaller sculpted leaves, and fewer smaller, sharper bat silhouettes." Its fix: "Reduce the number and prominence of the large amber disks and bats, vary ember size and focus by depth, and shift the suspended leaves away from large flat silhouettes toward smaller varied fragments." R3 part 2: "several large amber discs have uniform flat interiors and abruptly defined edges, so they look stamped over the much softer field of small lights" Its fix: "assign the large particles different depths and defocus them accordingly; soften their edges and vary their brightness across each disc" Tried: Round 13's R1 found the embers sparser, dimmer and cooler than approved, so `kinds3` made them denser and warmer (`bb54623`) and `fall_air3` let them rise through the whole dome with the row at `sizeMm [0.12, 0.75]`; the leaf row's `floats` went from 0.08 to 0.12 at the freeze (`9f6c179`). What the builders say is left: `kinds3`, "Embers: denser and warmer (seen at fall rest), still points where approved has more soft discs."; `fall_air3`, "Sparks softer and larger than the approved's points (the sprite is kinds3's drawing)."; on the bats, `kinds3`, "Bats: softer, darker, inside the glass (seen); the orange rim is too faint to see at hero size; no wing translucency." What to try next: fewer large discs, each with a soft edge and a brightness that falls across it, its blur taken from its depth (`CARD.spark` and `sparkClear` in `src/particles/draw/looks.ts`); a wider spread of ember size and brightness with depth; smaller bats (their count stays at four, the lowest the tuning range allows by decision 85, and is for Brandon to decide); a lower top size in the leaf row (`sizeMm [1.2, 3.8]`).

136. **The leaves are paper-thin planes that pass through the roof, the branches and the right pumpkin; the bats are flat silhouettes; near particles out of focus are hard-edged discs and pills.** (Round 16, R3 part 1 #7, major; `set-C-02.jpg`, crops 1, 2, 3, 6, native size crops of `fall-interior`; "also set-C-03.jpg crops 7, 10, 11". Also Round 13, R3 part 2 #6, minor, the bats; Round 10, R3 part 1 #2 and #4, major.) R3 part 1: "leaves are razor-thin flat planes that clip straight through roof shingles, branches, and the right pumpkin face; bats at the top are flat 2D silhouettes; and foreground defocused particles appear as hard-edged flat opaque discs and pills" Its fix: "give leaves slight 3D curl, thickness, and collision clearance, model full 3D miniature bats, and render foreground defocus with true optical depth of field instead of flat discs" Tried: `kinds3` raised the leaves' curl and their spread of tone (`bb54623`) and gave the bats a rim and focus; it could not judge the leaves, "with so few leaves in the hero", and it notes "One outline only (maple)". 138. **Item 77 again: the cottage reads front-on and toy-like, with large bright stones, flat roof tiles, a flat door and flat neon panes.** (Round 16, R1 #6, major; `set-A-02-a.jpg`, crops of the rest pair, crop 2 the cottage wall and roof; "in both keys". R3 part 1 #8, major; `set-C-02.jpg`, crop 6, native size crops of `fall-interior`; "also set-A-02.jpg crop 3". Also Round 10, R1 #6, major, and R3 part 1 #8, major; items 50 and 70.) Its fix: "Bring back the stronger left-wall perspective, finer rough masonry and shingles, recessed tall door arch, and clearer mullions around the concentrated green and magenta window light." R3 part 1: "the green and purple windows are flat neon fills with unlit grid lines and almost no stone frame bounce light, the wooden door is a flat painted plane with no relief, roof shingles show striped shader aliasing, and chimney bricks are out of scale with the wall stones" Its fix: "add recessed window glass with lit interior depth and frame bounce light, model beveled door planks and hardware relief, fix roof shingle aliasing, and unify masonry scale" Tried: `fall_mini3` did the season's share: the tone curve of the wall stones, the door, timber and roof tones (`fc1668e` to `c6d23ac`), "weathered slates with lit lower edges" (`269430d`), "panes with a dim room, a hot centre and grime" (`2945de7`). Its handover: "The cottage is smaller, more frontal and further left than the approved's; slates and wall stones are larger and paler at the gable. Shared layout and mesh." 208. **Polish round 2's likeness check of winter: 7 against a pass score of 9 (polish round 1: 6), with the storm still "a conspicuous upright whirlpool" and nine lines on the miniature, the glass, the collar, the base and the table.** (Polish round 2, R1, the likeness critic, once on the frozen build `9f4d94a`, engine `a103ddd4fdecc107`, on the season's two keys at the final tier; `reviewer_r97_w`, `gpt_6_2_sol`, a fresh critic on the family that judged winter in polish round 1, decision 125; the pack `out/work/packs/round-097/R1-winter/` holds the approved picture at rest and mid-shake (`-a`) beside the build's (`-b`), whole and in crops; the card is `scorecards/polish-2/R1-winter.json`: score 7, 1 severe, 8 major, 1 minor; polish round 1 gave 6.) Every line of the card, word for word. #1, severe, `set-B-01-b.jpg`, the storm from the left shoulder around to the bottom of the globe: "The shake reads as a conspicuous upright whirlpool with long, almost continuous white ribbons and a smooth horizontal band at the bottom. The target has a broader sweep made of much shorter, broken streaks and softly turbulent clouds, with more points of warm light carried inside the snow." Its fix: "Keep the intended concealment of the miniature, but break the long bands into shorter staggered trails at different depths, soften the tight swirl at left, and add scattered warmer glints in the rolling lower cloud." #2, major, `set-A-02-b.jpg`, the cottage roof, chimney, door and front wall (crop 2; also B): "The roof is wider and higher, the chimney sits higher, and the masonry reads as strongly shaded rounded blocks instead of the target's finer, flatter stonework. The broad dark door surround, larger window panes and brighter beadlike eave bulbs change the facade in both frames." Its fix: "Lower and narrow the roof and chimney slightly, use finer flatter stone with less contrast, tighten the arched door surround and window proportions, and reduce the size and intensity of the eave bulbs." #3, major, `set-A-02-b.jpg`, the tree crown, trunk and lights (crop 3; also B where visible): "Snow sits in separate chunky caps, and the crown is more sharply segmented. The trunk looks like a bundle of bright, straight orange ribs, and tightly packed round bulbs are conspicuous beneath each tier. The target has more integrated snow along the boughs, a darker, curved and knotted trunk, and softer individual lights." Its fix: "Blend the snow into the contours of the branches, give the trunk fewer and more naturally curving dark-grained limbs, and vary and soften the bulbs without reducing the intended storm cover in B." #4, major, `set-A-02-b.jpg`, the top and shoulders of the glass and the lower interior rim (crops 1, 2 and 5; also B): "The top dimple is larger and more conspicuous, the inner right reflection is thicker and softer at the end, and frost forms sharp, repeated fern-shaped patches over a relatively even pale rim. The target has a more defined reflection edge, deeper blue secondary reflections and frost that breaks up more organically into the rim and snowbank." Its fix: "Shrink the top mark, refine the silhouette of the white right reflection and restore the blue inner refraction. Break up the frost patches and blend them into the glass and uneven snowbank rather than leaving hard stamped shapes." #5, major, `set-A-02-b.jpg`, the glass seat, upper brass lip, and ice hanging from it (crops 4–5; also B): "The glass sits above a thick exposed brass ring and a second clean lip, reading as two separate rails. Irregular granular snow partly buries the finer seat in the target, and its icicles are more translucent, individually tapered and variably spaced." Its fix: "Lower the glass into a thinner collar, interrupt the exposed rails with more finely textured snow, and vary icicle outlines and clarity while bringing back the small transmitted highlights." #6, major, `set-A-02-b.jpg`, the carved apron and braided foot (crops 4–6; also B): "The front relief has a different silhouette, with fine scrollwork and a deeper pointed center instead of the fuller overlapping bronze leaves. The right side looks broadly powdered blue, and the foot trim is darker and more sharply outlined than the warmer, worn metal on the target." Its fix: "Rebuild the fuller leaf relief and pinecone grouping, concentrate the cool light near the right edge, and bring warm worn highlights and a softer transition back to the braided foot and the lower metal band." #7, major, `set-A-02-b.jpg`, the tabletop directly below the base and the snow at either side (crop 6 and full frame; also B): "The reflected gold foot becomes two clean parallel lines, with a particularly legible return at lower left. Side frost is flatter and whiter, spreading in graphic, jagged patches. The target reflection fades into dark blue and warm flecks and is broken by thicker, granular snow and delicate fernlike crystals." Its fix: "Diffuse and interrupt the reflected trim, recover the scattered amber and cool highlights, and replace the flat white patches with irregular granular clumps and fine frost fronds." #8, major, `set-A-02-b.jpg`, the pond, shore, and fence in front of the cottage (crops 2 and 5): "The pond reads as a flatter, squarer cutout with an abrupt dark bank and broad yellow sheen instead of a rounded blue, textured pool with a concentrated lamp glint. The fence has heavy rails and posts where the target has slender, individually readable uprights." Its fix: "Round and roughen the snowy bank, restore the fine cool-blue ice texture and compact warm reflection, and make the fence taller and finer with narrower rails, posts and balusters." #9, major, `set-B-02-b.jpg`, the lamp and adjacent cottage lights during the shake (crop 2): "A large diffuse yellow bloom centers on the lamp and washes across the cottage windows and pond. The target retains a distinct lantern light and a warmer, more diffuse glow spread low through the snow." Its fix: "Tighten the source glow around the lantern and windows, then spread the warmer scattered light lower through the moving snow without making the miniature more visible overall." #10, minor, `set-A-01-b.jpg`, the out-of-focus lights behind both shoulders (also B): "The high-right blue disc is larger and more saturated, and the warm light left of the globe is a little higher and broader. The targets have slightly finer discs and warmer rims on the upper-right pair." 212. **On Brandon's hosting a returning visitor would keep the old sounds after a new deploy: the sound files carry no version in their address, and `vercel.json` marks them as never changing for a year.** (Phase 5, found by the Builder at 22:45 UTC Nov 25 while reading `vercel.json` for the gate line on hosting; not a critic's issue; not run, read from the files. Unit: `globe`, the part `sound-engine` and the hosting files.) `kit/05-ARCHITECTURE.md`, "Hosting": `vercel.json` "sets long cache lifetimes for hashed files". The pictures' files are fetched with their hash in the address (`assets/winter/village-winter.glb?v=853e1261bb13949d`, from `assets/index.json`, which is itself fetched with `cache: 'no-cache'`), so a year is right for them. The sound engine fetches `audio/index.json` and each file it names (`sprite.mp3`, `amb-spring.mp3`, `music-winter.mp3` and the others) with no hash in the address and no cache rule of its own (`src/audio/index.ts`, `loadAudioIndex` and `raw`), and `vercel.json` gives `/audio/(.*)` the header `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. What follows on that host only: once a browser has heard the app, a later deploy with new sounds, which is what a review round or the cut to the approved soundtrack makes, would not reach it, and a new `index.json` beside old files, or the reverse, would set loop points and levels that do not belong to the files. This workspace's hosting is not that host and nothing says it reads `vercel.json`; the cache headers it sends itself were not read, because the published address answers 401 to this workspace. A first visit anywhere is right. Not changed now: the build of the review is frozen at `9f4d94a` and the phase gate is running on its clone. What to do, in the first task after the review, before any deploy to that host: give the sound index a hash for each file and fetch `index.json` as the asset index is fetched (the kit's way, since the year then belongs to hashed files), or as the smaller change set `/audio/(.*)` to `public, max-age=0, must-revalidate`; then load the app twice across a changed pack and read the requests.

213. **On a renderer where one frame takes longer than the probe's rest window, the probe writes "0.0" for the state at rest though it counted no frame there.** (Phase 5, found by the Builder at 22:50 UTC Nov 25 in the probe's run to its end on software GL; not a critic's issue; the cause is read from the code, the frame lists were not printed. Unit: `globe`, the part `probe`.) `src/app/probe.ts` gives each level `perf.probeSeconds` (15 s) and its last 5.4 s to the storm (one bar at 100 BPM, 2.4 s, and `shake.settleCheckSeconds`, 3 s), so the first 9.6 s are the rest. A frame is put in the rest's or the storm's list by the time spent after it, so a first counted frame longer than 9.6 s goes to the storm and the rest's list stays empty; `median` of an empty list is 0 and the table and the text block write it as "0.0 fps", the same as a measured rate under 0.05. Seen at all three levels in the run of 22:43 (rest 0.0 beside storm 0.1 at medium and low). Who is touched: only a machine that draws less than about one frame in ten seconds, where the pick is `low` either way and the page cannot be used; on any graphics card the rest list holds hundreds of frames. Not changed now: the build is frozen as `9f4d94a` and the phase gate is running on it. To do after the review, in the first task that touches the probe: write "not measured" (in the table and the text block) for a state with no counted frame, and count at least one frame in each state before a level ends.

214. **The Shake control fades out and back in each time its hint pulse ends: the pulse takes the place of the control's arrival animation, and when the pulse is taken off the arrival runs again from nothing.** (Phase 5, the fresh review before the review stop, must-fix 5; `final_pass_reviewer`, 23:15 UTC Nov 25, `scorecards/phase-5/final-pass-review.md`, picture `out/stills/phase-5/final-pass/phone_shake_control_missing.jpg`; not a kit critic's issue. Unit: `globe`, the part `interface`.) What it saw at 390 x 844: with the keyboard's focus on Shake, "the pill, its label and its focus ring are not drawn at all, while the marks and the sound button beside it are"; after a landing "the Shake pill is again not drawn; one still later it is back"; in two more runs the control's computed opacity read 0 at rest. Checked here in the code at 23:21 UTC, not on a screen: `src/ui/ui.module.css` gives `.shake` the animation `arrive` (0.7 s, from opacity 0 and 6 px lower) and `.pulse` sets `animation: glow` on the same element, so `arrive` leaves the list while the pulse runs and is a new animation when `.pulse` is removed (`endPulse` in `src/ui/index.ts`), and the browser plays it again from opacity 0. How long it shows on a graphics card is not measured: by the numbers in the file, about 0.7 s of fading in, after every hint (the first comes a few seconds after the first picture when nothing has been pressed). Round 19's R8 gave the interface 7 and did not name it. Not changed now: the build is frozen as `9f4d94a`, its gate is running, and both counts of rounds are used. To do after the review: keep `arrive` in the pulse's animation list (or run the pulse on an inner element), then record the first 15 seconds and a mark press on a real device.

NOT SEEN by anyone: a browser that does not know `rel=expect` (that it paints as before is an argument, not a look), what stands on the screen while the paint is held, a real phone, tablet or graphics card, the fade as motion, spring and summer in a takeover. 234. **The live app gives up its particle worker after a wait that counts the page's own stalls, and never takes a worker back.** (After the review, `framing_finisher`'s report of 11:04 UTC Nov 26 on its third job, the mend of item 231, merged as `4c2213c6`; not a critic's issue. `[globe]`.) MEASURED by it, phone layout 390 x 844, touch, medium, lavapipe: no frame of the page took 3.6 s; round a press the page's own callback takes 7 to 10 ms and the worker answers in 9 to 20 ms. At the press the browser ran the tap's events and then the frame callback in two idles running and handled no worker message; the second call found 3,616 ms waited and gave the worker up. That the answer lay unread is its inference: the probe sees handled messages only. The wait is counted in wall time between the page's own calls, so it holds the time the page itself was blocked: a real visitor loses the worker when an answer lies unhandled for 3 s (one frame of 3 s, or slow frames in a row with input waiting at the end). One real stall seen: the frame that prepares a season, 28.8 s under lavapipe; on a real graphics card not established. After the give up the page steps the particles itself for the rest of the visit: `fail()` ends the worker and the only start is in the constructor. Since `4c2213c6` that looks right (item 231), it costs the main thread the simulation. Its proposal, not built: give up only if the frame is still missing after the message queue has turned once, or cap each frame's share of the wait at about 250 ms. Given to `framing_finisher` as its fourth job at 11:04 UTC, 45 minutes. A second start of the worker after a give up stays out: it needs a new worker and client, the grids, a hand over and a policy. NOT SEEN by anyone: the fall back on a real graphics card; a stream of input over slow frames; a second shake after a fall back. Mended in main as `c33d6031` (merge of `agent/p6-framing` `cfabf185`, 11:54 UTC Nov 26, logged at 11:58): each call adds at most 250 ms to the counted wait, and a call that finds the count over the limit first posts a message to the page itself and gives up only if that came back and the frame is still missing. By its builder: tsc clean, 727 tests passed and 8 skipped. Still NOT SEEN: a real phone, a real graphics card; the second start of a worker stays out as said.

Either the page stands still through the click's 5 s under software drawing, and then the check's patience is wrong, or the control is covered, late or moved at that moment, and then a person's tap could miss as well. With `sound_finisher` since 11:58: the cause by measurement first, the check mended only if the first is true. Until then A2 is open and the soundcheck is not a pass. Mended in main as `08d44919` (12:30 UTC Nov 26, `tools/soundcheck.mjs` only, worked by `sound_finisher`): the first is true. Measured over seven runs of A2's steps with a recorder in the page: under software drawing the page gives frames 4.8 to 17.7 s apart after its first picture, and the click's time was sized from one pair of frames that fell on two quick ones in 4 runs of 7, so the click got its 5 s floor while the page stood still; in every sample the control was shown, enabled, uncovered and unmoved. The click now waits max(5 s, 6 times the slowest frame seen) and is tried up to 3 times, and again only when the page stood still through the wait; a control that is covered still reads open (tried with a covered copy). After the mend: A2 alone 6 passes of 6, the whole sound check 8 pass and 0 open (12:22 to 12:26). NOT SEEN: the second try running in the final code; a real graphics card, where frames are quick and the floor holds.

237. **At 3840 x 2160 and 24 samples, film B frames 4, 6 and 8 each hold 3 values that are not finite before the lens and the grade, so no master can be encoded from their chunk.** (After the review, 13:03 UTC Nov 26; found by the farm's rehearsal chunk of decision 152 on `farm_machine_2`, `bbc967b4`, engine `7bed76e87f414806`, the standard driver with the calibration line of the farm.) The masters' tool printed for each of the three frames: "NOT A NUMBER: film-b frame 4 holds 3 values that are no number in its mean, before the lens and the grade. Its chunk is marked NOT A NUMBER and no master is encoded from it." Frames 0 to 3, 5, 7 and 9 printed none. These are the first frames of the shot `open` (winter, the macro camera). Every judged still passes M1 at `hd` and the strict run passes, so it shows only with more pixels, other lens points or these frames. What is known of the path: the count takes infinite as well as no number; the sample target is a half float whatever the mean is, and a sample above 65504 is written as infinite and turns the mean to no number at the next sample; so the cause is either an open case of the arithmetic or one over-bright sample, a firefly, which would also flash for a frame through the lens in the films and in the live app. Not known yet: the place, the kind, the part, the cause, and how many of the film's 3600 frames, the opening's 867 and the loop's hold such a value. Worked by `farm_machine_3` as an engineer on `agent/p6-nan` from 13:10 (`tools/briefs/p6/nan-hunt.md`, in main as `9776d623`): where and what, why, the mend at the cause, a guard that bounds an infinite sample and never turns no number into a number, and a scan tool that the other farm machines run over the film before and after the mend. No frame of a master is drawn until the scan is clean.

## For Brandon to decide

Things only he can settle. Nothing waits on them.

1. Music and the sound tool's plan. The soundtrack is made with ElevenLabs on the Creator plan. Its terms allow commercial use of music "except film, TV, radio, and Studio Games" and do not define "film". The same plan is marked for individual use only: companies appear from the Scale plan up. So the terms do not clearly allow this music in a video a company posts on social media. One soundtrack candidate, `four-tracks`, is made and offered at the review anyway; `one-piece` could not be made (open item 188; this sentence said "both" until 23:22 UTC Nov 25, when it was set right). Your choices: approve as it is, move the account to a plan whose music terms cover it, or supply a track of your own, which replaces the generated music with no other change. Quotes: `references/terms/sound/QUOTES.md`.
- Item 1, added 2026-11-25 22:18 UTC: one candidate is made, not both. `four-tracks` exists and is the soundtrack of the review cut. `one-piece` has no music: its three takes were each heard as one mood from start to end, and the cue is out of takes (`audio.maxTakesPerCue` 3; open item 188). The choices above stand for `four-tracks`; a fourth `one-piece` take is one of the purchases in item 12.

2. The repo is public and the config expected it to be private. Because the sound tool's terms forbid making its output available as separate audio files, no generated sound file is committed. They live in the workspace and in the published app, and an archive is attached to the thread. If you make the repo private, say so and the kept sounds will be committed.
3. The approved images and Seedream 5 Pro. The terms that could be read do not clearly allow its output in a published video and on a public website: it depends on which route the image tool uses to reach the model, which is not published, and on the plan of this account. Nothing was changed because of this, as the kit says. New pictures that ship are made with models whose terms allow both. Quotes: `references/terms/images/TERMS.md`.
4. The plan of this account. The image tool's own terms allow commercial use of generated pictures on Enterprise Pro and Enterprise Max, and only personal use on individual plans. The account belongs to an organization, but the plan was not measured.
5. The hosting plan. Vercel's Hobby plan is for personal or non-commercial use only. A company portfolio piece may need the Pro plan. The limit behind `host.maxShippedMb` counts the source files uploaded by the command line tool, not the built site and not a deploy from Git, so the key is safe as it is and was not changed. Details: `references/terms/hosting/LIMITS.md`.

6. The hero framing and the lift of the shake (decision 29). The approved images show the globe with about 9 percent of the frame under its foot and 6 percent above the glass. The shake lifts the globe by a tenth of the frame's height in front of a locked camera, and the kit's checks do not let the camera stand further back than it now does. So the globe sits lower in the frame than in the approved images, with less of the surface in front of the base, and stays whole while it is shaken. The other choice is the approved framing with the top of the glass leaving the picture for about a second in each shake. It is one number in the config (`cameras.hero.aimHeightMm`, 74 now, about 66 for the approved framing).

- Item 6, added 2026-11-24 10:42 UTC: decision 45 lowers the lift and the tilt of the shake below the range the kit gives the Builder (expected about 6.5 mm and 6 degrees against the kit's 18 and 14), so that the lifted glass keeps about 5 percent of the frame above it, as the blockout critic asked. If you want the larger shake back, the choices are: accept the glass within half a percent of the top edge, let the camera stand further back than the fill check allows, or let the camera move with the lift.

7. The coding of the app's textures (decision 56, 2026-11-24 16:16 UTC). The kit asks for a compressed GPU format; measured here it made the files larger and the normal and height maps less exact, and the memory it would save is not needed (129 of 500 MB). The app ships near-lossless WebP instead. Say if the GPU format is wanted regardless, for phones with little memory; it is one more coding in the pack tool and one branch in the loader.

- Item 6, added 2026-11-25 11:12 UTC: the motion critics still read the shake as light, with a low lift and little tilt (Round 14, open item 127; Rounds 8 and 11 before it, open items 71 and 81). The larger shake is the choice described above; the Builder did not take it, because decision 45 was made for the blockout critic's ask and the fill check.

10. A hint that moves the globe (Declined 41 and 42, added 2026-11-25 17:38 UTC). Round 18's interface critic found that with no words on the page only the word on the Shake control says the globe can be shaken, and asked for the idle hint to rock the globe a little with a few flakes stirring, a second pulse, and a tilt or drag glyph on the first touch. The kit says the control "pulses once, softly", that it "never plays the shake by itself" and that there are "no instructions over the globe", so none of the three was built; the pulse is made plainer within the kit's word. Say if the globe may give a small rock by itself as the hint, or if a glyph may show once.

- Item 10, added 2026-11-25 21:44 UTC: Round 19's interface critic asks it again on the build with the brighter ring and the larger glyph (R8 #1, major, open item 204; Declined 44): "Play the hint sooner and synchronize one small side-to-side rock of the actual globe with a brief pulse on the control." When the hint plays is `live.hintAfterSeconds`, a value of the config that the Builder did not change.

11. A way to shake from the corners of a tablet (added 2026-11-25 21:44 UTC). Round 19's interface critic finds that on a tablet held upright the Shake control "sits nearly half a tablet width from either side grip, so it is not a natural thumb tap while holding the tablet by its edges", and asks to "add a tablet shake gesture from the lower corner areas so either thumb can trigger it without reaching over the globe" (R8 #2, major, open item 205). The kit names three ways to shake, the Shake control, the space bar and shaking a phone that has allowed motion, puts the controls "along the bottom edge" and asks for reach of a thumb on the phone only. A fourth way is a choice about the subject, so the Builder did not build one. Two ways it could go: two unseen press areas in the lower corners on the tablet size, or the Shake control moved toward one side on that size.

12. The sounds with no usable take, and what is left of the 10,000 credits (added 2026-11-25 22:18 UTC). Under your limit of 16:59 UTC the build spent 6,765 credits in 40 paid calls (effects 1,914, music 4,851); 3,235 are left, and no paid call was made after 18:11:27 UTC (decision 116). Eleven cues used their three takes and none was kept: `shake-winter`, `shake-summer`, `shake-fall`, `land-winter`, `land-spring`, `land-summer`, `land-fall`, `amb-winter`, `amb-fall`, `key-tap` and `music-one-piece`. In the film and in the app this means: only spring's shake has a sound of its own, every landing is the one glass ring, winter and fall have no ambience, the key presses of film A's prompt opening will have no sound (the opening is not in the review cut), and there is one soundtrack to choose, not two. At the prices seen, one more take of each costs 1,490 (shakes 29 each, landings 33 each, ambience 220 each, the key 6, the one piece 825); three more of each cost 4,470. The 3,235 left cover one more of each, or three of every effect and one more `one-piece` (2,820), not three of everything. Buying more takes is yours to ask for: a review round buys each cue you name up to three new takes with your words added to its prompt (`kit/03-METHOD.md` section 12, `audio.maxTakesPerCue`), so name the cues in your review notes and say whether the limit of 10,000 still holds. What the Builder would try for each, and why the three takes failed, is in the "Sound" section above and in `audio/prompts.json`.

13. The handle of the saved ElevenLabs credential in the public repo's history (added 2026-11-25 23:22 UTC, decision 128). Two scripts, `audio/run/music.mjs` and `audio/run/take.mjs`, held the handle of the credential you saved for ElevenLabs (`custom-cred:…@api.elevenlabs.io`) from their first commit `0fa0c590` (03:05 UTC Nov 25) until it was taken out at 23:22 UTC Nov 25. It is a pointer that this workspace turns into your key, not the key itself, and no key is anywhere in the repo or its history. Whether it could be used outside your own session was not tested. It is gone from the files but still in the history of a public repo. Your choices: leave it; delete the saved credential and save the key again, which gives a new handle and leaves the old one pointing at nothing; or have the history cleaned, which needs a forced push that this build does not make without your word.
